title: Who is The Man of the Hole?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the "Man of the Hole," an uncontacted indigenous man living alone in thatched huts in the Tanaru Indigenous Reserve in Rondonia, Brazil, believed to be the last survivor of his tribe after ranchers and loggers killed his companions. They cover FUNAI's Uncontacted Indians unit (CGIIRC, founded by Sydney Possuelo), the history of Brazil's Indian Protection Service and missionary contact, the debate over contact versus isolation (including an anthropologists' open letter and opposing views from Survivor International and FUNAI), the hole-trap huts, the 2011 video of him chopping a tree, the hired attempt to kill him, and the expanded protected area. They then survey other uncontacted peoples (North Sentinel Island, Korowai-type tribes in Papua, Old Believers in Siberia, Ozark isolated families), human safaris, and infanticide debates in Brazil. The episode closes with listener mail from Claire asking the hosts to be more positive about math.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about family resemblances and Josh's Instagram photo, then Josh introduces a HowStuffWorks article about the loneliest man on earth.

segments.title: The Man of the Hole and his isolation
segments.summary: The hosts describe the article's framing of the man as possibly the last of his people and the only person in his situation. They recount the 2011 and later videos of him near thatched huts in the Tanaru reserve in Rondonia, Brazil, and how ranchers and loggers likely slaughtered his tribe.

segments.title: FUNAI and Brazil's history of contact policy
segments.summary: FUNAI's monitoring role and its Uncontacted Indians unit, founded under Sydney Possuelo, are described. The hosts review the history from missionary contact through the Indian Protection Service and the 1960s exposé of abuses, and the policy shift to non-contact.

segments.title: Debate over contact versus isolation
segments.summary: Two American anthropologists wrote a letter urging planned, well-organized contact, which FUNAI, the UN and Survivor International opposed. The hosts discuss requirements such as cultural translators and year-long healthcare, and past missionary failures that led to deaths.

segments.title: Hole traps, hostilities, and the attempted killing
segments.summary: The hosts explain the holes inside his huts as possible protection, his farming and hunting habits, and the escalating hostility during contact attempts, including an arrow hitting an agent. After the protected area was expanded to about 42.5 square miles, ranchers hired someone to kill him; FUNAI found shotgun shells at a ransacked outpost.

segments.title: Movie treatment and Brazil's protection of his land
segments.summary: The hosts reflect on the man's story, comparing it to a Japanese straggler and imagining a Hollywood version, then discuss the Brazilian government's decision to let him live undisturbed on his land.

segments.title: Other uncontacted peoples around the world
segments.summary: The hosts note that about 50 to 80 or 120 uncontacted groups may live in the Amazon and survey other places: North Sentinel Island in India, the Korowai-type groups of Papua, Indonesia, and isolated families in the Ozarks. They discuss threats from resource extraction and population growth.

segments.title: Old Believers in Siberia
segments.summary: Soviet geologists found a family of Old Believers living in a remote Siberian cabin, dressed in burlap. The hosts discuss the group's history of leaving the Russian Church in the seventeenth century.

segments.title: Human safaris and infanticide debate
segments.summary: The hosts describe human safaris in Peru and nearby countries that take tourists to view uncontacted tribes, and an article on Brazil's struggle over infanticide among some isolated tribes versus constitutional rights.

segments.title: Listener mail: Claire on math
segments.summary: Claire, a math education student, asks the hosts to be more positive and encouraging about math. The hosts agree to take more care with their words.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh gives contact information for sending mail and social media links.
